title: Vortex-core Majorana coupling to a chiral edge in a $p_x+ip_y$ superconductor: Nonmonotonic spectral reorganization and coherent fermion-parity dynamics
abstract: We study how vortex--edge coupling reorganizes the low-energy sector of a finite two-dimensional \(p_x+ip_y\) superconducting disk as a function of the vortex--boundary separation \(d\) and examine what this reorganization implies for the parity memory associated with a prescribed vortex-core Majorana wave packet, a resource relevant to Majorana-based quantum operations. Bogoliubov--de Gennes calculations reveal nonmonotonic core--edge reorganization of the lowest positive-energy finite-disk eigenstate, with particularly rapid variation near \(d\simeq7ξ\), where \(ξ\) is the coherence length. To separate this eigenstate reorganization from the spectral representation of a prescribed state, we rigidly translate a centered-vortex core-reference packet to each fixed vortex position, restrict it to the target disk, and project it, without intermediate normalization, onto the particle-hole-complete low-energy subspace. For \(Δ_0/E_F=0.36\) and disk radius \(R=30ξ\), the resulting retained norm exceeds \(0.98\) at all six sampled separations, \(4.25\leq d/ξ\leq8.25\), while, depending on \(d\), the spectral measure is concentrated near zero energy, fragmented over several low-energy levels, or dominated by finite-energy weight. Correspondingly, the signed parity correlator displays slow temporal variation, rapid coherent dephasing, or sign-changing oscillations, with possible finite-size recurrences at later times. Thus a large retained norm does not by itself imply spectral concentration or persistent parity memory.
summary: This work analyzes the spectral reorganization in a superconducting disk containing a vortex by studying the coupling between the vortex core and the boundary. Using BdG calculations, the authors show that while the localized wave packet retains high norm, the resulting spectral properties and parity memory are highly sensitive to the vortex-boundary separation. This highlights that simple measures of wave function overlap are insufficient predictors of topological memory.
main_problem: The study investigates how the coupling between a vortex core and the boundary reorganizes the low-energy electronic spectrum of a finite 2D p_x+ip_y superconductor, and what this implies for the coherence and memory of Majorana wave packets.
main_result: A large retained norm of the reference packet does not guarantee spectral concentration or persistent parity memory, as the spectral measure and parity dynamics vary significantly with the vortex-boundary separation.
method: Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) calculations are employed, supplemented by analyzing regional coherence measures and parity correlators.
model_or_system: The system is a finite 2D p_x+ip_y superconducting disk containing a vortex, modeled using the grand-canonical mean-field Hamiltonian and solved via BdG equations.
key_observables: Nonmonotonic core-edge reorganization of eigenstates, retained norm of the reference packet, spectral measure (concentration/fragmentation), and signed parity correlator.
important_parameters: Vortex-boundary separation (d), superconducting gap ratio (Δ_0/E_F = 0.36), and disk radius (R=30ξ).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses a finite-disk approximation and an idealized reference preparation method for the vortex core packet.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate vortex geometry and image construction; other figures show the spectral measure and parity correlator varying nonmonotonically with the vortex-boundary distance d.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical system and Hamiltonian to calculating spectral reorganization via BdG, and finally analyzing the implications for parity memory using time-domain correlators.
why_interesting: The study of topological superconductivity, Majorana fermions, and spectral dynamics in confined geometries is highly relevant to understanding topological quantum computation and superconducting quantum circuits.
